# 19 Stop a comma inside a style value from discarding the whole diagram

## Outcome

`style Shape fill:rgb(255, 0, 0)` parses as one declaration whose value is `rgb(255, 0, 0)`,
instead of being split into three fragments, two of which are then reported as malformed and null
the entire document.

## Why this ticket exists

Found in round 3's review, verified against a real document: `parseStyleProperties` splits the
declaration list on every `,` before locating the `:`, with no awareness of parentheses. So
`fill:rgb(255,0,0)` becomes `fill:rgb(255`, `0`, `0)`; the last two have no colon, are reported as
`Unrecognized style declaration`, set `sawError`, and `parseClassDiagram` returns
`document: null`. One ordinary CSS colour — the most common spelling there is — discards the whole
diagram rather than styling one class.

Ticket 12's worker predicted the splitting flaw but judged it low-risk because no criterion on
this board needs comma-bearing values. The consequence is worse than "the value is wrong": the
document does not render at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `style Shape fill:rgb(255, 0, 0)` yields one property/value pair, value `rgb(255, 0, 0)`,
  with no diagnostic and a non-null document.
- [ ] The same holds inside `classDef`, which shares the splitter.
- [ ] Several declarations still split on the commas that separate *them*:
  `fill:rgb(1,2,3),stroke:#c00,stroke-width:2px` yields three pairs.
- [ ] Nested and unbalanced parentheses do not hang or silently swallow the rest of the list —
  decide what an unbalanced `(` does, document it, and test it.
- [ ] A segment that genuinely has no `:` is still an error diagnostic, as ticket 12 made it —
  this ticket narrows what counts as a segment, it does not stop diagnosing malformed ones.
- [ ] Every existing parser test passes unmodified.

## Test seam

`parseClassDiagram(source: string): ParseResult` — unit level, pure function, extending the
existing test file.
